audit.summary: This is not a content page — it is an 18-word language-router stub that points to Go (`using-randomness-go.md`) and TypeScript (`using-randomness-ts.md`) variants. It contains no definition of CRE randomness, no code, no specifics, and no metadata (no JSON-LD, no canonical, no dates). As served, it is effectively invisible to generative engines: there is nothing to lift, cite, or synthesize, so any engine that lands here will answer from parametric priors — a substantial hallucination risk for a security-sensitive topic like randomness. The single biggest opportunity is to give this URL a self-contained canonical answer-first summary of how to use randomness in CRE workflows, rather than leaving it as a redirect shell.

recommendations.title: Add page metadata / JSON-LD

antiPatterns: **Wall-of-nothing / stub page:** 18 words of body content; no substantive prose to retrieve.
**Path-as-title:** H1 is a raw URL path, harming entity resolution and title-based retrieval.
**Undated content:** no `dateModified` visible, weakening freshness signals.
offPageNotes: If this stub is intentional and the real content lives in `-go.md` / `-ts.md`, ensure those pages carry the canonical answer-first content and that this URL either redirects (canonical tag) or hosts the shared conceptual summary as a hub.
`llms.txt` is already referenced — good site-level signal; verify both language variants are indexed there.
Head metadata and JSON-LD are site-level template concerns; fixes here likely apply across all CRE guide pages.
